subjects.displayTitle: Government authority: public trust, service, and conscience
subjects.introduction: Wherever they live, Bahá’u’lláh tells His followers, they are to deal with the government of that country with loyalty, honesty and truthfulness, and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá gives the instruction daily substance: honest work in a public post, a word about no one but good. Such loyalty is a form of service, bound up with the welfare of the land, and it rests on a striking division: God has given the earth to the kings and has kept the hearts of His servants for Himself. That line forbids the believer to contend with rulers, and it keeps conscience free, so that obedience ends only where a spiritual principle such as the denial of one’s faith begins. Much of this was written to particular monarchs and in particular upheavals, and its praise belongs to those hours. Jesus’ answer about the coin, what is Caesar’s and what is God’s, raises a comparable question about distinct claims upon allegiance [1]. From here the inquiry opens into the mutual duties of government and people, the discipline of staying out of politics, and the limits of criticism.
subjects.arc: Open with truthful citizenship and public service, distinguish earthly authority and spiritual allegiance, explore justice and mutual responsibilities, then read historical counsels, political restraint, and conscience with attention to source status.

order.why: Open with loyalty, honesty, and truthfulness in every country.
Keep the parallel counsel for every country of residence.
shortened: In whatever country they live, let them act with utmost truthfulness, obedience, goodwill and trustworthiness toward that government.

order.why: Read truthful service and careful speech.
shortened: In whatever country you reside, serve that government with utmost truthfulness, obedience and goodwill. Never let any word except good pass your lips. This is established by the conclusive texts of the Blessed Beauty and is recorded and preserved in the Tablets.

order.why: Place upright conduct beside the recognition that all are created by God.
shortened: Know all to be created by God, and in whatever country you reside, be in complete obedience to the government under the shadow of the Lord's mercy, and with perfect willingness and love and uprightness and integrity be under the protection of the center of sovereignty. Strive as much as you can that the government of that region have complete satisfaction and security from you.

order.why: Make integrity in public employment concrete.
Keep service as an individual obligation.
Distinguish assigned public duties from political interference.
Keep reason and moral discrimination active in service.
shortened: Among the celestial characteristics of this sacred reality are reason and intelligence, and justice and fairness through heavenly inspiration. These divine powers have been bestowed to be put into action, not to be neglected and suspended. For instance, reason has been granted so that one may deeply contemplate and reflect on the beginnings and consequences of matters with penetrating thought, to distinguish between right and wrong actions, to perceive what is harmful and beneficial, to act with justice and fairness, and thus become a manifestation of the Most Merciful's grace and the dawning-place of the light of God's mercy.

order.why: Read the distinction between authority over people and attention to hearts.
Consider earthly rule and the divine domain of hearts.
Keep the same distinction in the Tablet to the Sultan reference.
Read the related reported formulation.
shortened: And likewise: "O friends of God and His trusted ones! Kings are the manifestations of power and dawning-places of might and wealth of God. Pray for them. Sovereignty over earth was granted to them, and He ordained hearts for Himself.

order.why: Place loyalty to just rulers within the Will and Testament.
Read encouragement to truthful service under the sacred texts.
shortened: Likewise, to constantly encourage and urge all the friends, in accordance with the decisive divine texts, to obey and serve the just throne of sovereignty, to show truthfulness and trustworthiness in service to His Imperial Majesty the just monarch, and to submit to the authorities of government.

order.why: Keep the instruction to counsel others in this practice.
Read justice and equity within the Treatise on Politics.
Connect citizenship with the betterment of character.
shortened: Let them willingly subject themselves to every just king, and to every generous ruler be good citizens. Let them obey the government and not meddle in political affairs, but devote themselves to the betterment of character and behaviour, and fix their gaze upon the Light of the world.

order.why: Hear the prayer for peace, common interests, and trustworthy service.
shortened: Thou knowest, O God, and art well aware that no intention have we save benevolence, and no purpose but peace and good will towards all humanity. We are broken-winged birds, bestow upon us new wings so that we become the cause of peace and tranquillity for the world of creation, the well-wishers of every soul, that we may serve the world of humanity, and strive in the common interest, obey all just leaders and labour with trustworthiness for the welfare of governments, for Thou hast made obedience, trustworthiness, truthfulness and submission towards governments a binding obligation.

order.why: Join integrity toward government to good faith toward all peoples.
shortened: It is incumbent upon us, rather, to obey the government with integrity, to speak with truthfulness, and act in good faith towards all the peoples of the world.

order.why: Read praise of friendliness and public obedience together.
shortened: Praise be to God, ye have behaved toward all peoples with truthfulness and friendliness, and toward the government, ye have evinced the utmost obedience and submission.

order.why: Read loyalty beside compassion for humanity.
Keep trustworthiness toward the country of residence.
shortened: However, the Baha'is sacrifice their lives for all humanity and worship mankind, but they are explicitly commanded that in whatever country they reside, they must show utmost truthfulness and trustworthiness toward the government of that land.

order.why: Consider friendship rather than hardship as the stated aspiration.
Read goodwill toward every people and government.
Place civic loyalty within the wider call to overcome prejudice and conflict.
Connect public service with nurturing humanity.
shortened: Therefore, O friends of Abdu'l-Baha, as far as ye are able, follow the path of the guides, sacrifice yourselves in the path of the Lord, be loving friends to all humanity, and become the nurturers of mankind. Be obedient and submissive to the just government, and become powerful servants to His Majesty the King, that ye may become the manifestations of divine confirmations and the dawning-places of eternal lights.

order.why: Keep kindness even toward enemies within the counsel.
shortened: They must show kindness to all people, even to enemies and ill-wishers, serve the throne faithfully, and obey the authorities with perfect good will, that they may become the cause of the ancient glory of that realm and the means of fame and renown for the people of Iran.

order.why: Read service alongside spiritual qualities and unity.
shortened: His good-pleasure lies in acquiring divine characteristics, holding fast to the ways of sanctification and self-effacement, showing humility and submissiveness before the loved ones of God, servitude at His exalted Threshold, diffusing the divine fragrances, uplifting the Word of God, fostering love and unity and oneness among God's loved ones, wishing well for all peoples and nations, remaining firm and steadfast in the Most Great Covenant, and showing sincerity and service to the government and seeking the satisfaction of the royal throne.

order.why: Explore education, industry, agriculture, women’s education, and civic service together.
Read industry and inventions beside honest conduct.
Consider capabilities directed toward the comfort of the realm.
shortened: In any case, the friends must show the utmost obedience and submission to the royal throne, and occupy themselves with service and loyalty, and demonstrate their capabilities in bringing comfort to the realm.

order.why: Keep education and character formation as public contributions.
shortened: Especially in the region of Kha, much effort and striving is needed so that souls may be educated and, with perfect obedience and submission to the government's commands, become the cause of education for all peoples, reform character, and encourage the acquisition of spiritual bounties and attributes of the Luminary of the horizons.

order.why: Read reciprocal duties of people and government.
Consider administration, laws, science, wealth, and future security.
Read the milk-and-sugar image amid government–people conflict.
shortened: Regarding what you wrote about the turmoil and disorder among other groups and the conflict between government and people and their disputes and arguments - it has been written repeatedly before that according to the counsels of the Blessed Beauty, government and people must mix together like milk and sugar, otherwise grave consequences will result.
They must obey the government and be well-wishers of all, neither associating with any party nor allying with any group.

order.why: Keep the related image of reconciliation and prosperity.
Consider protection of government and people together.
Preserve the contextual passage on reciprocal duties between generations.
shortened: The younger ones must show consideration and respect to their elders, and the elders must show kindness and care toward the younger ones. The youth must serve and honor the elderly, and the elderly must protect and look after the youth. These rights are reciprocal.

order.why: Distinguish public punishment from education that prevents crime.
Read the call for government to restrain violent religious leaders in its historical voice.
Preserve the question about concealing or reporting treachery without inventing an answer.
shortened: You had asked that since well-wishing toward government and nation is explicitly commanded as a religious obligation, and likewise covering faults is among the requirements of faith and certitude in the Divine Unity - in this case what should be done if someone commits treachery against the government and nation? Should it be concealed or reported to the government trustees and leaders of the national assembly?

order.why: Consider public administration of marriage and divorce.
Read petitioning within the stated ethic of obedience.
Keep composure and deliberation in presenting public desires.
Read the association of authority with outward security.
shortened: That which is necessary today is obedience to government and adherence to wisdom. In truth, the reins of preservation, tranquility and assurance outwardly lie within the grasp of governmental authority. Thus hath God willed it and thus hath He ordained it.

order.why: Join public service and wisdom to progress.
Keep wisdom and obedience as paired obligations.
shortened: O My loved ones! Observing wisdom and obedience to government are among God's binding commands. Hold fast to them, as bidden by One Who is a sincere counselor, trustworthy.

order.why: Consider the stated protective role of government in communal gatherings.
shortened: In all gatherings, if it is a meeting for conversation and fellowship, some mention must be made of the praiseworthy qualities of those in authority and the kindness of the Pasha. And if they are meetings for remembrance and devotion, certainly at the end prayers for good must be offered, as they have rights of protection and support. If there were no government, not a moment's peace would be possible for the servants, and no created being would find rest even on mountain peaks.

order.why: Keep the source’s account of physical comfort and civil order.
Read the connection drawn between obedience and national honor.
shortened: Therefore the more the people show obedience to the government and respect for the throne of sovereignty, the more they have in reality preserved themselves, maintained their own respect and honor, and considered the glory of the nation as a whole.

order.why: Keep the historical comparison of civic motives in its own voice.
shortened: The only group of people which today submitteth peacefully and loyally to the laws and ordinances of government and dealeth honestly and frankly with the people, is none other than this wronged community. For while all sects and races in Persia and Turkestan are absorbed in promoting their own interests and only obey their governments either with the hope of reward or from fear of punishment, the Baha'is are the well-wishers of the government, obedient to its laws and bearing love towards all peoples.

order.why: Consider willing service distinguished from compliance through fear.
Read integrity in office alongside the counsel amid clerical cruelty.
shortened: In the Cause of God, this obedience to the government is an obligatory and a mandatory command based on the definitive Text, and is applicable even in cases where the ignorant clerics inflict cruelties upon the friends the likes of which were perpetrated by Shaddad, Nimrod, Pharaoh, or the despicable Yazid, instances of which these clerics have already committed.

All state officials whether young or old must with utmost purity, virtue and perseverance be satisfied with their small allowance and stipend and be pure and chaste, and exert themselves with absolute integrity and justice and with total trustworthiness in the service of their revered King for were a soul to act disloyally towards a just government, he acteth disloyally towards God Himself, and were he to serve such a government, he verily serveth God.

order.why: Hear gratitude for protection from oppression in its setting.
Read the report of a monarch’s intention to establish just laws.
shortened: O ye Hands of the Cause! According to reports received, His Imperial Majesty—may God perpetuate his sovereignty—has, of his own volition and with sincere intention, resolved to establish just laws, deliver Iran from chaos and disorder, and lay in that desolate realm the foundation of complete civilization. These sacred intentions of His Imperial Majesty are truly worthy of gratitude and deserving of the appreciation of all his subjects.

order.why: Keep the particular release from imprisonment and response of gratitude.
Read praise of protection for the oppressed as a historical judgment.
shortened: May they be faithful servants to His Majesty the just King and worthy bondsmen to His Highness the pure-natured Crown Prince, for today the royal government is the protector of the oppressed and the healing balm for the wounds of those who suffer tyranny. The hands of the fierce are shortened and the sword of cruelty is sheathed.

order.why: Retain the particular ruler’s praise and the source omission.
shortened: Praise be to God, the ruler of that country is pure of heart, just and kind, knowing and wise, a leader and judge and protector of the oppressed.
You must guide all the divine friends to be well-wishers of this sovereign.

order.why: Keep gratitude and prayer for increasing equity in their setting.
shortened: In fine, forget ye not the justice and magnanimity which, from the Centre of sovereignty and from the attendants of the royal court, have been shown unto you. Ever offer prayers of good-will, and beseech from the Threshold of the Divine Unity victory and assistance for His Majesty the Shah. In very truth, during these latter years he hath exercised the utmost justiceâ€"nay, even favor and solicitude. Pray ye, therefore, and at the court of God offer supplication and entreaty, that day by day the equity of his sovereignty and the majesty of his kingship may increase.

order.why: Read the prayer for justice, protective laws, and equality.
Preserve the supplied date of the call to gratitude.
Keep the instruction to submit a letter of thanks.
Read gratitude for justice through loyalty and prayer.
shortened: Therefore, with utmost humility and supplication, seek divine confirmation for His Imperial Majesty, and in gratitude for justice, demonstrate complete faithfulness, obedience and loyalty to the government.

order.why: Consider service to rulers who care for their subjects.
Keep the stated reciprocity between justice and truthful service.
shortened: Therefore pray for good night and day, and in accordance with the decisive divine texts, you must serve with perfect sincerity, trustworthiness and steadfastness. For whoever betrays His Majesty the just King has betrayed the Truth, and all his deeds are wasted, for justice requires a corresponding truthfulness and service.

order.why: Read praise of redress and justice in the particular counsel.
shortened: O friends of God! Among the requirements of faithfulness and necessities of purity is obedience and submission to the commands of His Majesty the King, for praise be to God, he is justice-spreading and redress-granting.

order.why: Retain the address concerning a kind and just sovereign.
Keep service to the just government.
Addresses obedience in relation to just government and protection of rights.
Preserve the particular praise of a kind leader.
Read praise of the heir-apparent in its historical setting.
Preserve gratitude toward the named office of Amir.
Keep the interpretation concerning a particular sovereign attributed.
shortened: Call all to obedience and submission to His Imperial Majesty the just sovereign, for this illustrious personage is mentioned in the Great Announcement that he would become crowned and sovereign, and he is assisted and confirmed, victorious and triumphant according to the explicit text of the Most Holy Book - and this statement sufficeth the worlds.

order.why: Read the counsel concerning the designated government.
shortened: According to the Command, those beloved ones and chosen ones must act in whatever way brings joy and gladness to the designated just government.

order.why: Hear prayer and sincerity together.
Keep the instruction to pray for the just king.
shortened: Similarly, it is obligatory upon all the friends of God, by the decisive sacred text of the All-Merciful, to pray wholeheartedly for His Majesty the just King and to make great efforts in obedience and submission.

order.why: Read the address to friends and handmaids concerning service.
Keep willing service and goodwill together.
Retain the address to faithful subjects.
Read prayer for the crowned head’s confirmation.
shortened: The friends of God should pray morning and evening, with heart and soul, seeking divine confirmation and success for the eternal glory of this well-conducting crowned head. Therefore, guide the friends day and night to show obedience, truthfulness and trustworthiness at the threshold of sovereignty, for this is a religious obligation of the party of truth.

order.why: Join prayer to composure and dignity.
shortened: Today the greatest obligation of the loved ones of God is obedience and submission to the government, composure and dignity in all conditions, well-wishing toward the throne of sovereignty, and prayers for the just monarch.

order.why: Keep the short prayerful obligation.
shortened: It is incumbent upon us to pray for the government, to be obedient and submit ourselves.

order.why: Read kindness to humanity beside prayer for the Emperor.
Hear the devotional affirmation of pure intentions.
shortened: Yet Thou knowest, O my God, that we have no purpose except Thy good-pleasure and no intention except loyalty, and that in Thy Holy Book Thou hast commanded us to obey every sovereign with manifest truthfulness and to maintain pure intentions in obeying his mighty command.

order.why: Read counsels during upheaval in the Holy Land.
shortened: Therefore, the divine friends should not become sorrowful and grieved upon hearing of certain events and upheavals in the Holy Land, and should not show the slightest weakness in their pure intention, sincerity of purpose, and well-wishing toward these two eternal governments. They should, with utmost trustworthiness and sincerity, engage day and night in offering prayers for good on behalf of these two eternal governments.

order.why: Keep the prayer for protection from calumny.
shortened: Be ye faithful and obedient servants to the throne of the Iranian monarchy, and be ye submissive, humble and lowly before the royal court. Act according to the teachings of Baha'u'llah in this regard, and pray for us, beseeching with utmost humility at the Threshold of the Divine Unity, that these wanderers may perchance remain protected and preserved from the arrows of calumny of the wolves.

order.why: Retain the address concerning a new monarch.
shortened: In any case, the divine friends must serve the throne of sovereignty of this new monarch with utmost sincerity and goodwill, and be fully obedient subjects, and always supplicate at the Divine Threshold that this royal threshold may endure and that divine assistance and victory for the crown may be continuous and established.

order.why: Read the request to present earlier texts about two governments.
Keep the specific proposal to clarify the teachings to an ambassador.
Read the historical circulation of the Treatise on Politics.
Keep the invitation to observe the collected counsels.
shortened: Now observe how much praise of government exists in the Tablets and how much command to obey and be faithful to the throne of sovereignty.

order.why: Consider the source’s restriction on speech about worldly leaders.
Keep the particular concern over public gatherings in its setting.
shortened: After this matter was presented in the Most Holy Court, this word was issued from the Source of Command - exalted be His glory: Write that the government has had and will have no concern with your inner beliefs and religion, whether you deny religions or recite the Quran. The government has no objection, but gatherings cause commotion and are contrary to the government's wishes, for from the beginning, governments have neither been aware of this Cause nor are they now, and throughout history they have witnessed corruption arise from gatherings.

order.why: Distinguish goodwill toward officials from involvement in political affairs.
shortened: Exercise complete sincerity and good-will toward the government authorities and His Majesty the Shah, and maintain obedience and good intentions, but absolutely do not interfere in political affairs.

order.why: Read avoidance of political interference alongside absence of treachery.
shortened: However, the depths of the sea are clear, meaning the reality of these servants is goodwill toward the government, absence of treachery, perfect sincerity and kindness toward all the world, and avoidance of even mentioning politics, let alone discussing or interfering in it.

order.why: Place detachment beside the stated obligation of obedience.
shortened: They are heedless and detached from all save the mention of God, and by explicit text are obedient to the government of the sovereign, and by strict command are submissive to the throne of kingship.

order.why: Read the particular service needed in Azerbaijan in its broader context.
Keep the response declining political questions.
Preserve the warning about political troublemakers as an attributed judgment.
Read goodwill toward both sides and avoidance of conflict.
shortened: The divine friends must absolutely not make excuses and not be self-willed in the slightest degree. They must act according to the instructions, which are that they should obey the government and be well-wishers to both sides and as much as possible be the cause of peace and tranquility, but absolutely not interfere in conflict and strife.

order.why: Keep neutrality and kindness toward all parties.
shortened: But it was written to all that they must show complete obedience to the government and remain neutral and show kindness to all parties but never interfere in disputes and conflicts.

order.why: Consider wisdom in avoiding alarm.
shortened: Among the requirements of wisdom is that one must observe the government and not act in any way that would cause offense or alarm, for all are explicitly commanded to obey and submit to the government.

order.why: Retain the warning to a newspaper with its explicit reference to time and circumstance.
Read the reported distinction between public office and sedition.
shortened: Nevertheless, a Baha'i may hold a political office and be interested in politics of the right type. Ministers, state officials and governor-generals in Persia are Baha'is, and there are many other Baha'is holding governmental positions; but nowhere throughout the world should the followers of Baha'u'llah be engaged in seditious movements.

order.why: Keep the reported distinction between religious and employment responsibilities.
Read the separate source’s version of that response.
Consider the reported military analogy as an analogy of obedience.
Keep the reported wartime assertion in its historical voice.
Preserve the polemical comparison of communities as the source’s characterization.
Read the historical claim about parties in Iran as attributed.
shortened: Indeed it is as you wrote - among all the existing parties in Iran, the only one that shows obedience and submission to the government is the Party of God, for they are commanded, not by implication but by explicit text, to obey the government and show loyalty to the state, even to the point of sacrificing their lives for the eternal glory of the human world.

order.why: Keep the source’s related declaration of confidence attributed.
Retain the affirmation of truthfulness within the Covenant.
Read the obligation across independent and constitutional government.
Keep obedience and goodwill joined.
Read the brief affirmation of goodwill toward sovereignty.
shortened: They are obedient to the government and well-wishers of the throne of sovereignty.

order.why: Retain the command concerning government officials.
shortened: It is incumbent upon the friends of God to obey the commands and ordinances of His Majesty the King. Whatever he commands, they must obey. Likewise, they must show complete submission and obedience to all government officials.

order.why: Read the concise general obligation.
shortened: In any case, the friends must show perfect obedience and submission to the government.

order.why: Keep its explicit textual basis.
shortened: By explicit text we are submissive to the royal throne and humble before the authorities.

order.why: Join loyalty, goodwill, and trustworthiness.
shortened: You must, in accordance with the divine text, remain loyal, well-wishing, trustworthy and obedient to the royal throne.

order.why: Read the source’s account of happiness in both worlds.
Preserve its theological account of disloyalty.
Read the connection drawn between authority and obedience to the Messenger.
Keep the explicit restriction on contrary action.
shortened: Whatever royal command is issued, obey and submit to it. Do not take any action, either outwardly or inwardly, that contradicts the explicit will of the sovereign, for this is categorically forbidden.

order.why: Read the emphatic instruction against qualifying this command.
shortened: The friends of God must demonstrate the utmost obedience and submission to the government in accordance with the divine texts, and not deviate a hair's breadth from the good pleasure of His Imperial Majesty. The decisive text declares that the friends must be well-wishers, truthful, obedient and submissive to the government. Let no one interpret otherwise, exercise independent judgment, or introduce any qualification, and this is the station of those near to God.

order.why: Keep the further statement against reinterpretation.
Retain the emphatic statement concerning public and private conduct.
Read the reported reply about unjust rule with its question and source status visible.
Turn to the supplied letter’s distinction concerning spiritual principle.
shortened: ...we must do two things -- shun politics like the plague, and be obedient to the government in power in the place where we reside. We cannot start judging how a particular government came into power, and therefore whether we should obey it or not. This would immediately plunge us into politics. We must obey in all cases except where a spiritual principle is involved such as denying our Faith. For these spiritual principle we must be willing to die.

order.why: Close with the supplied distinction between administrative restrictions and fidelity in belief.

questions: How do truthfulness, public service, and goodwill give substance to the idea of loyalty?
What does the distinction between earthly authority and the domain of hearts help clarify?
How do the passages about justice and mutual responsibilities affect your reading of obedience?
What changes when praise of a particular ruler, a general teaching, and a reported conversation are read with attention to their different settings and authority?
How does the exchange about Caesar and God illuminate questions of civic allegiance and religious conscience?
How might these readings prompt further inquiry into public responsibility, peaceful petition, political non-participation, and the preservation of belief?

references.label: 1 · Mark 12:13–17 · Caesar and God
references.note: Read the question about tribute, the coin, and Jesus’ response in the King James Version. Compare the distinction between claims of earthly rule and claims of God with the compilation’s language of authority and hearts. Attend to the exchange’s adversarial setting and avoid treating the two traditions as identical accounts of government.

subjects.displayTitle: Independent investigation: seeing, reasoning, and seeking together
subjects.introduction: Look at the sun through another person’s eyes, Bahá’u’lláh warns, and you will never recognise it. On reaching maturity each of us is to investigate, freed from both love and hate, hearing with our own ears and seeing with our own eyes; the Báb put it more briefly still, that every soul must distinguish truth from falsehood for itself. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá called reason and the eye of investigation a trust squandered when we simply inherit our fathers’ beliefs. Such investigation is no licence for private opinion: it goes with justice, fairness and a pure heart, and applies to rejection as much as acceptance. The Buddha’s counsel to the Kalamas, to test teachings by their fruits and the judgement of the wise rather than by report or preference, is a venerable companion to this discipline [1]. The way onward leads into the condition of search, into blind imitation and how it is undone, into the harmony of science and religion, and into the liberty of thought a community must protect if conviction is to mean anything.
subjects.arc: Begin with personal responsibility and fair inquiry, develop reason and disciplined attention, widen the search across traditions, then connect shared truth-seeking with fellowship, revelation, scholarship, and freedom of conscience.

order.why: Explore individual faculties and responsibility at length.
shortened: God has given man the eye of investigation by which he may see and recognize truth. He has endowed man with ears that he may hear the message of reality and conferred upon him the gift of reason by which he may discover things for himself. This is his endowment and equipment for the investigation of reality. Man is not intended to see through the eyes of another, hear through another's ears nor comprehend with another's brain. Each human creature has individual endowment, power and responsibility in the creative plan of God. Therefore, depend upon your own reason and judgment and adhere to the outcome of your own investigation; otherwise, you will be utterly submerged in the sea of ignorance and deprived of all the bounties of God.

order.why: Open with maturity, personal inquiry, and freedom from both attachment and aversion.
Make independence apply to rejection as well as acceptance.
shortened: O Hussein in Sad, He is the Mighty! It hath been known to that honored one that the purpose of creation hath ever been and shall ever be the knowledge of God, and this knowledge dependeth upon the recognition of His servants who perceive the Truth through their own vision and heart and nature, for imitation sufficeth not, whether in acceptance or rejection.

order.why: Hear the Bab’s concise statement of personal responsibility.
Read justice and the searching eye together.
Keep the Seven Valleys’ invitation to inquiry.
shortened: O My brother, consider these matters in the spirit of enquiry, not in blind imitation. A true wayfarer will not be deterred by the impediment of words, nor daunted by the sway of insinuations.

order.why: Consider the difference between conscience and dependence on another’s perceptions.
Read personal examination as using a divine bounty.
Keep the public address on seeing and hearing for oneself.
shortened: Another new principle revealed by Bahá’u’lláh is the injunction to investigate truth—that is to say, no man should blindly follow his ancestors and forefathers. Nay, each must see with his own eyes, hear with his own ears and investigate the truth himself in order that he may follow the truth instead of blind acquiescence and imitation of ancestral beliefs.

order.why: Read the same invitation in the reference to the Bayan.
Consider the sun seen through one’s own eyes.
shortened: Behold the sun with your own eyes - thus have you been commanded in all the Tablets, if you be of those who know. Were you to behold it through the eyes of others, by My life, you would never recognize it - this is a certain truth.

order.why: Read the qualification concerning justice and fairness with care.
shortened: O Mihdi! He Who is the Beloved of the world, the Guide, speaketh thus: Today all are commanded to behold with their own eyes; hearing and seeing from others sufficeth not, except for such souls as have freed themselves from their vain imaginings and have cleaved to the lights of justice and fairness.

order.why: Keep understanding and discernment directed toward revelation.
Consider investigation as the basis of an informed voice.
Read the reported community of truth-seekers and the demand for reasons.
Keep the reported search for why and wherefore.
shortened: Imitation in religion is not allowable. We must find the 'Why' and the 'Wherefore' for ourselves.

order.why: Ask how reason is needed even to understand sacred texts.
Read the reported balance of reason and science.
Keep the related reported injunction to weigh claims.
shortened: Therefore man must be free of all conceptions and ancestral traditions. Everything must be weighed on the scale of science and reason, for religion and reason are one and can never be separate.

order.why: Consider reason as an endowment and examine inherited interpretations.
shortened: God has created man and endowed him with the power of reason whereby he may arrive at  valid conclusions. Therefore, man must endeavor in all things to investigate the fundamental reality. If he does not independently investigate, he has failed to utilize the talent God has bestowed upon him.

First, man must independently investigate reality, for the disagreements and dissensions which afflict and affect humanity primarily proceed from imitations of ancestral beliefs and adherences to hereditary forms of worship. These imitations are accidental and without sanction in the Holy Books. They are the outcomes of human interpretations and teachings which have arisen, gradually obscuring the real light of divine meaning and causing men to differ and dissent.

order.why: Read impartial investigation across forms of belief.
shortened: Forms must be set aside and renounced; reality must be sought. We must discover for ourselves where and what reality is. In religious beliefs nations and peoples today are imitators of ancestors and forefathers. If a man's father was a Christian, he himself is a Christian; a Buddhist is the son of a Buddhist, a Zoroastrian of a Zoroastrian. A gentile or an idolator follows the religious footsteps of his father and ancestry. This is absolute imitation. The requirement in this day is that man must independently and impartially investigate every form of reality.

order.why: Keep the reported invitation to experimental inquiry from foundations.
shortened: In the Manifestation of the Holy Divine Manifestations, these hearts are purified from outward effects. Every soul with the eye of insight wishes to gain understanding in the mysteries of divine and material matters. This is how hearts begin to flow. But if a person limits their thoughts to what scholars have said and written, it is of no benefit. These must be set aside and matters investigated experimentally from their foundation; one must search for truth, then new matters will become evident and clear.

order.why: Read the reported appeal to multiple standards with its source setting visible.
shortened: The rule, then, which we should adopt in our investigations, is this: In determining every question we should refer it to these four standards, and a conclusion which is supported by the verdict of all we should accept; any other we should regard as uncertain.

order.why: Preserve the reported quotation about doubt as an attributed statement.
Give sustained attention its place in understanding.
Keep expanding knowledge and continuing thirst together.
shortened: One's sphere of knowledge should be expansive, and in all conditions one should seek awareness. The more one drinks, the thirstier one becomes - not that with one sip one should display self-sufficiency.

order.why: Read the reported search into realities and mysteries.
Consider investigating each subject without preconceived ideas.
Keep the call to impartiality and freedom from prejudice.
Join penetrating vision to a pure heart and fairness.
shortened: Now observe with penetrating vision, with a pure heart, and with complete fairness, and reflect, that the truth may become clear to you and the path of God which hath appeared in truth may become manifest, and that you may find yourself possessed of clear certainty.

order.why: Read the open and unbiased approach to signs of revelation.
shortened: Verily I say, this is the Day in which mankind can behold the Face, and hear the Voice, of the Promised One. The Call of God hath been raised, and the light of His countenance hath been lifted up upon men. It behooveth every man to blot out the trace of every idle word from the tablet of his heart, and to gaze, with an open and unbiased mind, on the signs of His Revelation, the proofs of His Mission, and the tokens of His glory.

order.why: Consider detachment from what has been seen and heard.
shortened: Whosoever desireth to attain unto the recognition of the Lord of this Day must needs detach himself from all that he hath seen and heard, and must, with an eye sanctified from the film of vain imaginings, observe within the very Essence of Truth, and ponder upon His signs.

order.why: Read the call to tear away veils of imitation.
Keep the reported warning about inherited superstition.
Read equal consideration of religions without attachment or aversion.
Consider careful attention beyond ancestral assumptions.
Keep the concise counsel to abandon tradition and seek truth.
shortened: Second is the independent investigation of truth - all traditions must be abandoned and truth sought.

order.why: Read inquiry as undoing blind imitation.
Retain the reported prohibition of imitation.
shortened: Thus all are captive to traditions, following the traditions of their forefathers. But Baha'u'llah declared that imitation is not permitted - there must be investigation of truth.

order.why: Keep the separate reported formulation of personal investigation.
Read seeking reality beyond hereditary forms.
Keep the invitation addressed to every individual.
shortened: First among the great principles revealed by Him is that of the investigation of reality. The meaning is that every individual member of humankind is exhorted and commanded to set aside superstitious beliefs, traditions and blind imitation of ancestral forms in religion and investigate reality for himself.

order.why: Examine hearsay and hold to what inquiry finds true.
Read the separate report of that counsel.
Keep the interview’s insistence on continuing unbiased inquiry.
Read the interview’s definition of independent investigation.
Retain the brief interview statement.
Include the preceding question about the tenets of faith.
Include the reported question before its call to seek realities across religions.
Calls for investigation at the divine source rather than judging truth through nations’ conduct.
Consider water, fruit, flowers, and wine beyond attachment to their vessels.
Read the lamp and rose images in the account of spiritual cycles.
Seek reality wherever and through whomever it appears.
Keep the reported invitation to seek signs of illumination.
Let differing opinions become an occasion for encounter.
Join inquiry to love and fellowship.
shortened: Let no one assert and insist upon his own mere opinion; nay, rather, let each investigate reality with the greatest love and fellowship.

order.why: Distinguish promoting reality from promoting personal opinions.
Read gratitude for an assembly willing to examine and accept truth.
Consider release from prejudice as a condition of collective inquiry.
Read truth through knowledge, fellowship, and recognition of one humanity.
Consider the claim that undivided reality can unite seekers.
Read the reported distinction between reality and conflicting traditions.
Explore the foundations of religions as a place of reconciliation.
Keep the reported relationship between truth and oneness of belief.
Read the account of inquiry overcoming contention.
Retain the reported comparison with Theosophical seekers in its setting.
shortened: We both (Theosophists and Bahais) have abandoned all dogmas in our earnest search for truth. But look at the tribes and nations of the world--why are they seething with contention? Because they are not seeking truth. Truth is one. It admits of absolutely no division and accepts neither limitations nor boundaries.

order.why: Keep the related claim about reality and imitation.
Read fairness and inquiry amid competing national claims.
shortened: Therefore a person must see things through his own eyes and not through the eyes of others and investigate the truth of the matters by himself and not rely on the words of others. Every group has its own claim, and each nation has its own proclivities. If people would consider matters with equity and investigate the veracity of things by themselves, then no discord would remain, and all would embrace one another in unity and oneness.

order.why: Keep the separate formulation of that social hope.
Join investigating reality to love and unity.
shortened: Second, that truth or reality must be investigated; for reality is one, and by investigating it all will find love and unity.

order.why: Consider results that come from seeking reality beyond varied thoughts.
Read the particular counsel to Green Acre.
Consider a gathering seeking the foundations of religion.
Place investigation within the Tablet to the Hague’s vision of renewal.
shortened: Among these teachings was the independent investigation of reality so that the world of humanity may be saved from the darkness of imitation and attain to the truth; may tear off and cast away this ragged and outgrown garment of a thousand years ago and may put on the robe woven in the utmost purity and holiness in the loom of reality.

order.why: Read its role among teachings for preventing war.
shortened: There have issued, from His mighty Pen, various teachings for the prevention of war, and these have been scattered far and wide.

The first is the independent investigation of truth; for blind imitation of the past will stunt the mind. But once every soul inquireth into truth, society will be freed from the darkness of continually repeating the past.

order.why: Consider independent inquiry as a path to human oneness.
Join truth-seeking to the elimination of prejudice.
Read the particular service of overcoming racial and other prejudices.
Keep the reported hope for broadened minds and love of humanity.
Read seeing and hearing personally as a contribution to collective reform.
Place inquiry beside the oneness of humanity.
Read it within the wider enumeration of teachings.
shortened: The teachings of Baha'u'llah are the light of this age and the spirit of this century. Expound each of them at every gathering.
The first is investigation of truth,
The second, the oneness of mankind,
The third, universal peace,
The fourth, conformity between science and divine revelation,
The fifth, abandonment of racial, religious, worldly and political prejudices, prejudices which destroy the foundation of mankind.

order.why: Consider the more extensive list, including science, equality, language, and justice.
Keep the reported relationship of human oneness, inquiry, and religion’s foundations.
shortened: At such a time as this Baha'u'llah proclaimed the first principle of His mission and teaching -- the oneness of the world of humanity. His second announcement was the investigation of reality; the third was the oneness of the foundations of the divine religions.

order.why: Read the reported conjunction of Gospel practice and Baha’i principles.
Keep the historical account of Baha’u’llah’s sufferings and religious unity.
Read the reported succession of Prophets as promulgators of truth.
Consider inner meanings beyond names.
shortened: They must awaken the peoples and nations of the world and free them from dogmas and imitations. They must pass beyond the world of names and fix their gaze on realities and inner meanings.

order.why: Read the call to new patterns of thought.
Keep the synagogue address’s invitation to investigate.
Retain the reported appeal to uncover reality beyond dogmas.
Read multiple paths and the source’s affirmation of one Truth together.
shortened: When a person of insight enters the path of spiritual wayfaring, after purifying and sanctifying the soul from all that God loveth not, multiple paths appear and he traverses them. This is why they have said "The paths to God are as numerous as the breaths of created things." However, if through God's grace the eye is blessed with the light of truth, it will be observed that the Truth is one, the Path is one, and the Cause is one.

order.why: Examine the evidence of light rather than the objection about its timing.
Keep recognition from being delegated to others.
Read the invitation to compare a Tablet and other writings personally.
shortened: We pass over all that hath appeared in this Revelation; read but a single Tablet from among the wondrous Tablets, and likewise the writings of others, and judge for yourselves. Should anyone arise with fairness, he will undoubtedly, after hearing the divine verses, instantly turn toward the realm of oneness.

order.why: Consider the Causes of Christ and Baha’u’llah with one’s own faculties.
shortened: If thou wishest to discover the mysteries of the divine Kingdom, move beyond the world of imitation, observe with thine own eyes, hear with thine own ears, and carefully consider the Cause of Christ and likewise the Cause of the Blessed Beauty.

order.why: Read meditation on what is manifest today.
shortened: Leave behind whatsoever you have heard and listened to in the past, and meditate upon that which is manifest today, that perchance you may drink and give others to drink of the choice wine of steadfastness, which is more precious than all the known and mentioned rivers.

order.why: Keep the Bab’s counsel concerning scripture and just, unworldly persons.
shortened: Look to the matter of religion: whatever agrees with the Book and the Practice of God, accept it with certainty and act upon it. When any new matter arises, present it to just and unworldly persons - if they confirm it, then accept it; if not, then do not.

order.why: Read the reported concern about information from biased sources.
Preserve the recipient’s journey through societies to a stated spiritual goal.
Hear the acknowledgment of a seeker’s discovery.
Keep the particular praise for investigating reality.
shortened: O two servants of the Kingdom! Your letter arrived and was clear proof that, praise be to God, you have been freed from the darkness of vain imaginings and have reached the center of truth. You have been delivered from antiquated traditions that tell tales of ancient times, and you are investigating reality.

order.why: Read inquiry alongside teaching.
Hear encouragement to a serious investigator.
Keep gratitude for the capacity and desire to investigate.
shortened: At the time of each Manifestation of God the people were heedless and ignorant of the truth except for a few who investigated and understood the divine words. The same is true today. So thank God that you have been endowed with capacity and desire to investigate the truth.

order.why: Read sustained inquiry through a lifetime.
shortened: They were awake and vigilant, enamored with truth and attracted to mysteries. During their lifetime they never rested nor relaxed, they investigated truth and strove to discover the mysteries of existence.

order.why: Place independent sight beside courage, joy, and perseverance.
Retain the report’s national characterization as a historical observation.
Keep the related reported praise of receptivity attributed.
Read seeing, hearing, and purity of heart in the reported address.
Retain the brief description of seekers.
Hear the prayer for increasing fervor and clear vision.
Close the linked readings with prayer for sight free of imitation.
shortened: Therefore, O my God, I beseech Thee by Thy Most Great Name and Thy Most Ancient, Most Perfect Word to purify the hearts of Thy loved ones from the veils of fancy and imitation, that they may know Thee with their own eyes and behold Thy beauty with their own sight.

order.why: Open the supplied readings with responsibility that cannot be transferred.
Connect investigation to analysis, philosophy, and science.
Consider investigation as a human right in the supplied statement.
Read the protection required for freedom to know.
Keep the explicit protection of conscience from coercion.
Close with friendship across differences of opinion.

questions: How can we recognize imitation in both our acceptance and our rejection of a claim?
Which habits of mind and heart make independent inquiry more reliable?
How might personal investigation draw upon other people’s knowledge without surrendering responsibility for judgment?
What similarities and differences emerge between the Kalama Sutta’s attention to ethical consequences and the methods of inquiry in these readings?
How can a belief in the oneness of truth sustain friendship while people reach different understandings?
What would a community committed to both thoughtful conviction and freedom of conscience make possible for its members?

references.label: 1 · Kalama Sutta, AN 3.65 · Inquiry and ethical consequences
references.note: Read the Kalamas’ uncertainty about competing teachers and the Buddha’s examination of harmful and beneficial qualities in Thanissaro Bhikkhu’s translation. Compare the tests of experience, consequences, and the judgment of the wise with the compilation’s personal responsibility and freedom from prejudice. The discourse also questions mere inference or preference; it is not a license to accept whatever one already believes.

subjects.displayTitle: Human distinction: powers that call for responsibility
subjects.introduction: The measure of a human being, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says, is whether others are more at ease because of you; comfort kept for oneself is something cattle and birds attain as well. That is a bracing place to begin, because it refuses to let human distinction rest on cleverness alone. The same mind that discovers the roundness of the earth, sends ships under the sea and voices across continents, can hate more terribly than any animal and, with its inventions, kill thousands at a stroke. The animal is nature’s captive; the human being alone wrests the sword from nature’s hand, and that freedom cuts both ways. Behind the familiar ladder of mineral, plant, animal and human lies a claim about the soul: a power of discovery not reducible to sharper senses, a capacity for virtue, and an image of God realised only through education and effort. Aristotle’s account of the powers of living things offers a philosophical foil for weighing those claims [1]. The journey continues into the mind’s power over nature, the higher and lower natures within each person, and the long questions of human evolution.
subjects.arc: Begin with service and the danger of destructive ingenuity, explore rational and spiritual capacities, examine the sources’ language about nature and development, then return to education, virtue, and responsible action.

order.why: Consider intellectual attainment alongside virtues and spiritual perception.
shortened: It is clearly evident that while man possesses powers in common with the animal, he is distinguished from the animal by intellectual attainment, spiritual perception, the acquisition of virtues, capacity to receive the bestowals of Divinity, lordly bounty and emanations of heavenly mercy. This is the adornment of man, his honor and sublimity.

order.why: Open with distinction measured by bringing comfort to others.
Join love and human oneness to the question of distinction.
Acknowledge that human cruelty can exceed animal ferocity.
Read the reported warning that inventions can multiply destruction.
Ground the inquiry in a shared human substance and personal exertion.
Connect human reality with knowledge and betterment of the world.
shortened: Man has been and continues to be among the greatest signs of God, and has come from the realm of non-existence into the court of existence for the knowledge and betterment of the world.

order.why: Read the divine image as qualities of perfection in the address to children.
shortened: O ye young Baha'i children, ye seekers after true understanding and knowledge! A human being is distinguished from an animal in a number of ways. First of all, he is made in the image of God, in the likeness of the Supernal Light, even as the Torah saith, 'Let us make man in our image, after our likeness.' This divine image betokeneth all the qualities of perfection whose lights, emanating from the Sun of Truth, illumine the realities of men.

order.why: Introduce the source’s account of bodily, growing, sensing, and mental powers.
shortened: Man is the most distinguished species in that he combines the perfections of all three classes--that is, he possesses a material body, the power of growth, and the power of sensation. Beyond the mineral, vegetable and animal perfections, however, he also possesses a special perfection of which other created things are bereft, namely, the perfections of the mind. Thus man is the noblest of all existing things.

order.why: Read the related philosophical classification.
shortened: Hence God has created man as the sum of all realities. For instance, the degrees of existence are either mineral, vegetable, or animal, and man is the distinguished species that combines the perfections of the mineral, vegetable and animal kingdoms.
Thus in man there exists a comprehensiveness--that is, he combines all the perfections of the mineral, vegetable and animal kingdoms.

order.why: Add the capacity to comprehend universals.
shortened: In the human degree, the mineral perfection exists, the vegetable perfection exists, the animal perfection exists, and beyond these, mental perfection exists which discovers the realities of things and comprehends universals.

order.why: Keep the concise public-address formulation.
shortened: The human kingdom is replete with the perfections of all the kingdoms below it with the addition of powers peculiar to man alone.

order.why: Consider shared physical conditions and the rational soul.
Retain the bodily resemblance and asserted distinction.
shortened: Man is like the animal in physical structure but otherwise immeasurably separated and superior.

order.why: Keep the reported emphasis on consciousness.
shortened: The physical body of man is like that of the animal, the only difference being on the level of consciousness.

order.why: Read the extended account of arguments concerning human and animal powers.
shortened: Although man shares the same outward powers and senses in common with the animal, there exists in him an extraordinary power of which the animal is deprived.

It is clear then that if man did not possess a power beyond the animal powers, the animal would perforce surpass man in significant discoveries and in the comprehension of realities. It follows from this argument that man is endowed with a gift, and possesses a perfection, which is not present in the animal.
Moreover, the animal perceives sensible things but cannot perceive conceptual realities.
It is therefore clearly established that man is endowed with a power of discovery that distinguishes him from the animal, and this power is none but the human spirit.

order.why: Explore the Tablet to Dr Forel’s account of discovery and relative perception.
shortened: The animal is the captive of nature and cannot transgress the rules and laws thereof. In man, however, there is a discovering power that transcendeth the world of nature and controlleth and interfereth with the laws thereof.

In like manner all other beings, whether of the mineral, the vegetable or the animal world, cannot deviate from the laws of nature, nay, all are the slaves thereof. Man, however, though in body the captive of nature is yet free in his mind and soul, and hath the mastery over nature.

Relatively to the plant, the reality of man, his power of hearing and sight, are all supernatural, and for the plant to comprehend that reality and the nature of the powers of man's mind is impossible.

order.why: Consider the reported passage from visible appearances to rational inference.
shortened: Perceiving and reflecting upon visible things, he realizes the reality of unknown things. When a man gazes at the earth he sees it as if it were level, but by his perception he finds that it is a globe. This power of perception can never be found in the animal kingdom; but man by this power can prove that the sun is a center and that the globe and other bodies revolve around it.

order.why: Keep the related report concerning speech and conceptual understanding.
shortened: Man, in this station, is endowed with the power of speech, but man can comprehend most important things, while animals cannot. It is impossible for an animal to know whether the earth is a sphere or a plane, while man can know. It is impossible for an animal to know that the sun is the center around which the earth rotates, because an animal can only know things which can be seen or felt, but man can also understand what he senses by the intellect.

order.why: Read the reported distinction between sensation and intellectual apprehension.
Consider the public address’s distinction between body and intellection.
Read ideal conclusions and animal tendencies within the same address.
shortened: The station of man is great, very great. God has created man after His own image and likeness. He has endowed him with a mighty power which is capable of discovering the mysteries of phenomena. Through its use man is able to arrive at ideal conclusions instead of being restricted to the mere plane of sense impressions. As he possesses sense endowment in common with the animals, it is evident that he is distinguished above them by his conscious power of penetrating abstract realities.
Verily, God has created the animal in the image and likeness of man, for though man outwardly is human, yet in nature he possesses animal tendencies.

order.why: Keep the short affirmation of discovery.
Connect rational power with education toward universal thought.
shortened: Man has a sacred power beyond the confines of the senses. The power of the rational mind is the power of the soul over the senses. This cycle is radiating love and the bestowals of God are descending like unto rain. Man's glory lies in the difference between him and the animals. In Persia a small child who has been taught to think universally can talk with the learned.

order.why: Read intellect, will, faith, and scientific acquisition as divine gifts.
shortened: Man is endowed with ideal virtues -- for example, intellection, volition, faith, confession and acknowledgment of God -- while nature is devoid of all these. The ideal faculties of man, including the capacity for scientific acquisition, are beyond nature's ken. These are powers whereby man is differentiated and distinguished from all other forms of life. This is the bestowal of divine idealism, the crown adorning human heads.

order.why: Consider spiritual potential and the image of God.
shortened: God has created all earthly things under a law of progression in material degrees, but He has created man and endowed him with powers of advancement toward spiritual and transcendental kingdoms. He has not created material phenomena after His own image and likeness, but He has created man after that image and with potential power to attain that likeness. He has distinguished man above all other created things. All created things except man are captives of nature and the sense world, but in man there has been created an ideal power by which he may perceive intellectual or spiritual realities.

order.why: Hear the prayerful account of knowledge and guidance.
shortened: O God! O Thou Who hast shone upon luminous realities with the dawning of knowledge and guidance, distinguishing them from all other created things through this supreme gift, and making them encompass all things - perceiving the realities of beings and bringing forth hidden mysteries from the realm of the unseen into the world of effects, singling out whom Thou pleasest with Thy mercy!

Among all created things, He has distinguished humanity with the supreme gift and blessed it with the bounty of the Concourse on High. This supreme gift is the greatest guidance, whereby human reality becomes the niche of this lamp.

order.why: Place universal divine signs beside the particular human gift.
Keep the human being as a sign of divine bounty.
Read the reported purpose of human attainments in existence.
Explore discovery and craftsmanship in the account of natural law.
shortened: Man is able to resist and oppose nature inasmuch as he discovers the natures of things and, by virtue of this discovery, has mastery over nature itself. Indeed, all the crafts that man has devised proceed from this discovery. For example, he has invented the telegraph, which connects the East and the West. It is therefore evident that man rules over nature.

order.why: Consider the contrast between physical strength and mental power.
Read bodily vulnerability and intellectual mastery together.
Follow the reported examples of flight, heat, light, and extended senses.
shortened: For man alone of all the animals is not governed by the conditions in which he finds himself. He has no wings, but he does not submit himself to this fact; he makes wings and conquers the air. He has no fins, but he conquers the sea. He conquers the night by creating for himself light; the cold by making heat; his limited senses by supplementing and extending them. He assails Heaven itself that he may rise to God, his Father and Creator.

order.why: Read natural gifts beside the power to uncover mysteries.
shortened: However, although humans may not have a full share and abundant portion of these natural gifts, in the divine world they are the manifestation of endless favors, the niche of the light of reality, the bright mirror of divine beauty, the manifestation of heavenly gifts, the dawning-place of divine lights, and possess a sacred power that encompasses all created things. This is why they discover the realities of things, exercise dominion over nature, bring forth nature's mysteries from the realm of the invisible to the visible, break nature's might, destroy nature's law, disrupt nature's system - sometimes soaring through the air, sometimes racing across the surface of the sea, sometimes riding beneath the sea.

order.why: Examine the public address’s part-and-whole argument and language about nature.
shortened: Man is superior to nature and makes nature do his bidding. Man is a sensitive being; nature is without sensation. Man has memory and reason; nature lacks them. Man is nobler than nature. There are powers within him of which nature is devoid.

It may be claimed that these powers are from nature itself and that man is a part of nature. In answer to this statement we will say that if nature is the whole and man is a part of that whole, how could it be possible for a part to possess qualities and virtues which are absent in the whole?

order.why: Keep the technological examples within their stated theological argument.
shortened: All live within the bounds of natural law, and nature is the ruler of all except man. Man is not the captive of nature, for although according to natural law he is a being of the earth, yet he guides ships over the ocean, flies through the air in airplanes, descends in submarines; therefore, he has overcome natural law and made it subservient to his wishes.
The truth is that God has given to man certain powers which are supernatural.

order.why: Read the reported association of ideality and spirit.
shortened: Man is possessed of the emanations of consciousness; he has perception, ideality and is capable of discovering the mysteries of the universe.
But man wrests the sword of dominion from nature's hand and uses it upon nature's head.
Man transcends nature, while the mineral, vegetable and animal are helplessly subject to it. This can be done only through the power of the spirit, because the spirit is the reality.

order.why: Keep consciousness and freedom from nature in the public address’s terms.
Consider the dual description of animal embodiment and conscious being.
Read the reported role of spiritual illumination.
shortened: The animal cannot escape the law of nature, whereas man may control it, for he, containing nature, can rise above it.
The power of the Holy Spirit, enlightening man's intelligence, has enabled him to discover means of bending many natural laws to his will.

order.why: Keep the Holy Spirit and intellectual discovery connected in the source.
shortened: Likewise the Holy Spirit is the very cause of the life of man; without the Holy Spirit he would have no intellect, he would be unable to acquire his scientific knowledge by which his great influence over the rest of creation is gained. The illumination of the Holy Spirit gives to man the power of thought, and enables him to make discoveries by which he bends the laws of nature to his will.

order.why: Read the reported claim for knowledge’s distinctive power.
Retain the short formulation about natural laws.
Keep the movement from bodily danger to spiritual power.
shortened: On all sides he is surrounded by dangers and difficulties, against which his physical body alone cannot cope. If a man looks at the world around him, he will see how all created things are dependent and are captive to the laws of Nature.
Man alone, by his spiritual power, has been able to free himself, to soar above the world of matter and to make it his servant.

order.why: Consider the contrast between bodily smallness and mental power.
Read the emphatic statement of humanity’s station.
Keep will-power directed toward constructive achievements.
Read the address’s rational and evolutionary arguments in their historical setting.
shortened: In brief, the traces of reason are manifest and resplendent in man, and man is man by virtue of this rational power. Thus the animal world is other than the human world.

The proof is that man, in the embryonic state, is worm-like; afterward he passes from form to form until he assumes this present shape. Yet when he was worm-like, he was still man; his species had remained preserved. This very link which they say is missing is the proof that man was never an animal.

order.why: Consider the commentary’s claim concerning species and growth.
shortened: But some of the philosophers of Europe think that one species evolves into another species. For example, that the animal evolved until it became a human being.

Nay, rather evolution and growth take place within the same species. For instance, the seed of man gradually develops, passing through the stages of embryo, fetus, infant, childhood, and adolescence until mental maturity is attained. All the while it has progressed within the same species.

order.why: Read the embryonic analogy for change of form and continuity of species.
shortened: But from the beginning of his existence man has been a distinct species. This is similar to the embryo of man in the womb of the mother: it possesses at first a strange appearance; then this body passes from shape to shape and from form to form until it appears in the utmost beauty and perfection. But even when it possesses in the womb of the mother a strange form entirely different from its present shape and appearance, it is the embryo of a distinct species and not of an animal: the essence of the species and the innate reality undergo no transformation at all.

order.why: Examine the arguments about antecedence, potential, and development.
shortened: The first answer to this argument is that the antecedence of animals to man is not a proof that the essence of the human species was altered or transformed or that man came from the animal kingdom. For so long as it is acknowledged that these different beings have appeared in time, it is possible that man simply came into existence after the animal.

To summarize: Just as man progresses, evolves, and is transformed from one form and appearance to another in the womb of the mother, while remaining from the beginning a human embryo, so too has man remained a distinct essence--that is, the human species--from the beginning of his formation in the matrix of the world and has passed gradually from form to form. It follows that this change of appearance, this evolution of organs, and this growth and development do not preclude the originality of the species.

order.why: Consider gradual appearance of capacities in the universal order.
Keep the reported account of successive degrees and potential humanity.
Read the argument about completeness of creation and the perfect human being.
shortened: So if we were to imagine a time when man belonged to the animal kingdom, that is, when he was merely an animal, existence would have been imperfect. This means that there would have been no man, and this chief member, which in the body of the world is like the mind and the brain in a human being, would have been lacking, and the world would thus have been utterly imperfect.
Now, what we mean by "man" is the complete human being, the foremost person in the world, who is the sum of all spiritual and material perfections, and who is like the sun among all created things.

order.why: Retain the stated rational conclusion about human origins.
Keep the source’s Egyptian examples and permanence-of-species claim attributed.
shortened: The specificity and essentiality of things are permanent and changeless; only within the limits of a particular species do progress and decline occur. For example, the human species and human nature have been and will forever remain preserved and protected. As can be observed, the mummified ancient human bodies that have been extracted from the pyramids of Egypt, though five thousand years have passed since their death, have not changed or altered even by a hair's breadth from the human form. Likewise the images of animals that exist in Akhmim, Egypt are exactly like existing animals - a monkey is a monkey with that ugly appearance, a human is human with that beautiful, pleasing countenance. There is no altering in God's creation.

order.why: Read the seed analogy within the source’s account of eternal species.
shortened: His species is eternal, and this everlasting reality has neither beginning nor end. What Western philosophers say about human evolution - that man has come from the mineral, vegetable and animal kingdoms and reached this station through growth and development - is mere fancy, for the human species is ancient. Perhaps on this earth it was initially like a seed, then progressed and reached the station of "the best of creators." But that seed which gradually developed was the human species, not animal. Therefore this species is ancient and was originally the noblest of earthly creatures.

order.why: Distinguish recurrence of species in the discussion of reincarnation.
shortened: With respect to the species, however, return and recurrence are plainly visible in material realities; that is, the trees which in years past bore leaves, blossoms and fruits will in the years to come bear the same leaves, blossoms and fruits. This is called recurrence of species.

order.why: Keep the distinct species and mirror imagery together.
Preserve the comparison of gems, fruits, and capacities in the account of spiritual stations.
Read the reported contrast between scientific and prophetic accounts as attributed rhetoric.
Keep the reported invitation to attend to spiritual affiliation.
Consider the animal spirit in the source’s classification of soul and mind.
shortened: The animal spirit is that all-embracing sensory power which is realized through the composition and combination of the elements. When this composition disintegrates, that spirit likewise perishes and becomes non-existent. It may be likened to this lamp: When oil, wick, and flame are brought together and combined, it is lit; and when this combination disintegrates---that is, when the constituent parts are separated from one another---the lamp also is extinguished.

order.why: Read the reported account of animal sensation and mortality.
Keep the reported distinction concerning divine spirit.
shortened: The superiority of man over the rest of the created world is seen again in this, that man has a soul in which dwells the divine spirit; the souls of the lower creatures are inferior in their essence.

order.why: Read the related report concerning awareness of God.
shortened: Humans outwardly resemble animals - the difference between humans and animals is that humans possess spiritual powers while animals are deprived of them. Humans are aware of God while animals are unaware.

order.why: Consider the capacity to apprehend divine teachings.
Preserve the reported answer and visible source omission.
Examine the reported question about limits of perception.
Read the rhetorical comparison with philosophers of nature.
Consider the reported cow example as an argument about inference from nonperception.
Keep the humorous philosophical comparison in its source’s voice.
Read the related reported challenge to materialism.
Examine the address’s argument about the limits of sensory knowledge.
Consider the taste of salt and sweet water as an analogy for inward difference.
shortened: We must not look at the worldly condition, but at the truth in it--the divine truth--because if we look only at the outward form of man, how can we distinguish him from the animal, because we find them eating and doing the same things; but when we give attention to the spirit in man, we find it is far different from the animal. When you look at water, salt and sweet, you cannot tell the difference, but when you taste the water, you can distinguish.

order.why: Read the idealized bird imagery as a rhetorical question about purpose.
shortened: If the aim were this physical life only, then this creation would be in vain and men would not have more honor or be nobler than other creatures.

The greatest of sensual pleasures, beauty of appearance and freedom are found among the animals. Birds excel all in sensual pleasures, for they build nests on the loftiest branches and breathe the purest air.
They have no grief, regrets, aspirations, ambitions, quarrels, contentions, wars or massacres.
If the purpose of existence is sensual life and pleasures, then animal and man are equal. Happiness and pleasure are rather the possession of the bird and not those of distressed and sorrowful men.

order.why: Keep the related reported comparison of material needs.
shortened: The life of animals is more simple than that of man. Animals have all their needs supplied for them. All the grasses of the meadows are free to them. The birds build their nests in the branching trees and the palaces of kings are no so beautiful. If earthly needs are all then the animals are better supplied than man.

order.why: Consider the flock and beehive example.
Read the reported bee-and-ant image in its argument for ideal virtues.
Examine captivity to desire in the moral analogy.
Keep material aspiration within the source’s account.
Read the reported warning against intellectual self-satisfaction.
shortened: Like the animals they walk on the surface of the earth and would not allow their minds to be illumined by the eternal verities of the universe. What they have - though infinitesimally small - pleases and satisfies them. They seek no further and go not beyond the questions of bread and meat.

order.why: Retain the reported question about merely living, eating, and dying.
shortened: Man must so adorn himself with good attributes, attractions and divine characteristics that he may become the cause of the illumination of the world of humanity; otherwise his life will be a burden on him.
What difference will there be between him and the animals, who are born, live, eat and die!

order.why: Bring education into the account of human development.
Explains humanity’s need for education by contrasting destructive human behavior with animals.
Preserve the reported judgment about ignorance as the source’s characterization.
shortened: What is the distinction between man and animal - wherein lies the difference? It is in reason, knowledge and learning. Ignorant peoples and nations are lower than animals.

order.why: Connect reason and capacity with responsibility to acquire virtue.
Read the reported distinction between knowing and choosing the good.
shortened: For example he knows that drinking is a bad habit, gambling is a vice, robbery is a crime, still you find him committing one or all of these things - simply because these things belong to the natural, unregenerated state, they are 'part' of nature and as he is another 'part' of nature - (but unenlightened by the heavenly Light) he is attracted to them and takes pleasure in the companionship of the wicked. Under such circumstances the animal's actions are excusable because he is not endowed with the intelligent Faculty but man is responsible on account of his superior creation and reasonable powers.

order.why: Keep the severe moral comparison and cited verse attributed.
